hook.en: A large *company* may have lakhs of shareholders, yet it can sign contracts, own factories and go to court in its own name. How can a business be a person in law?
hook.kn: ದೊಡ್ಡ ಕಂಪನಿಗೆ ಲಕ್ಷಾಂತರ ಷೇರುದಾರರಿರಬಹುದು, ಆದರೂ ಅದು ತನ್ನದೇ ಹೆಸರಿನಲ್ಲಿ ಒಪ್ಪಂದ ಮಾಡಿ, ಕಾರ್ಖಾನೆ ಹೊಂದಿ, ನ್ಯಾಯಾಲಯಕ್ಕೆ ಹೋಗಬಹುದು. ವ್ಯವಹಾರವೊಂದು ಕಾನೂನಿನಲ್ಲಿ ವ್ಯಕ್ತಿಯಾಗುವುದು ಹೇಗೆ?

body.en: A *company* is an association of persons formed for carrying on business, with a separate legal entity, limited liability and perpetual succession. It is an artificial person created by law under the Companies Act, 2013, managed by an elected board of directors, and its formation is lengthy and costly. The common seal, once compulsory, is now optional.

narration.en: A company is an artificial person created by law. It is separate from the shareholders who own it.

say.en: A company is an artificial person created by law. It is separate from the shareholders who own it.
It can own property and sue in its own name, its members have limited liability, and it has perpetual succession.
Limited liability in numbers: if you hold shares of ₹10,000 fully paid, that is all you can lose.
Private and public companies differ in members, share transfer and inviting the public.
A private company restricts share transfer and cannot invite the public; a public company can do both.
And a One Person Company has just one member, but still enjoys limited liability.

narration.en: Let us work through this case together. Rohit holds 1,000 shares of ₹10 each in a public company, on which ₹6 per share has been paid. The company goes into liquidation with heavy debts. What is the most Rohit can be asked to pay?

say.en: Let us work through this case together. Rohit holds 1,000 shares of 10 rupees each in a public company, on which 6 rupees per share has been paid. The company goes into liquidation with heavy debts. What is the most Rohit can be asked to pay?
Face value per share equals 10 rupees; paid equals 6 rupees; unpaid equals 4 rupees per share.
Unpaid amount equals 1,000 times 4 rupees equals 4,000 rupees.
Liability is limited to the unpaid amount; his personal property is safe.
So the answer is 4,000 rupees.
